A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CogAlpha research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–C are readable, and the equations, tables, figures and relocated analyses can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original CSI300 prediction and backtesting results, component ablations, threshold sensitivity and alpha-evolution measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations across additional stock markets, training methods and prediction horizons, plus hyperparameter and generated-factor analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 changes adaptive guidance from the top two valid alphas to two randomly selected valid alphas. Appendix B.4 additionally introduces plateau-based early stopping alongside fixed-generation evolution. The core hierarchy, quality checker, fitness selection and evolutionary operators remain; expanded checker descriptions and prompts mainly disclose existing components.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from CSI300 large-cap Chinese equities to CSI500 smaller Chinese companies, U.S. S&P500 stocks and Hong Kong HSI/HSCI stocks. Appendix B.1 and Table 5 establish actual evaluations across these additional populations and markets.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all 19 original baselines and adds evaluated AutoAlpha (Kou et al., 2024) and AlphaAgent comparisons. These introduce directly relevant automated alpha-mining frameworks absent from v1's reported comparisons. Both works were already cited in v1, which called the Kou method AutoGPT.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce a 30-day CSI300 target, Ridge factor combination, additional market-specific chronological splits and controlled variations of population and generation settings. Appendix A.4 specifies a lower S&P500 MI floor, 0.012 versus CSI300's 0.02. Existing CSI300 dates, metrics and backtest costs remain unchanged; newly disclosed rolling-training and factor-count details do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: The original component ablation, threshold sensitivity and liquidity-evolution example are retained. v2 adds an eight-configuration AgentMarketCycle sensitivity study covering parent-pool size, generation count and sub-cycle length (Table 4), three elite-factor cases with training/test measurements (Listings 4–6), and a computational-cost comparison in Appendix B.5.

E5.justification: Appendix B.6 newly states that reported outcomes follow a single round of factor mining and discusses LLM randomness. v1 supplies no corresponding run-count statement. Neither version reports repeated-run confidence intervals or significance tests; this is additional disclosure, not evidence of changed replication.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 and component-ablation scores remain, while v2 adds comparator, sensitivity, cross-market, runtime and elite-factor results. New 30-day CSI300 LightGBM results are IC 0.0886 and RankIC 0.1243; the original 10-day values remain 0.0591 and 0.0814, so these are different settings. v2 also acknowledges Random Forest's higher RankICIR, 0.4385 versus 0.4350, and revises the strong single-factor finding to refer to absolute correlations.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly defines the plateau statistic delta = mean(curr) - mean(prev), with termination when delta <= 0.001. This is a limited mathematical specification of the stopping rule. Existing factor and evaluation-metric equations are otherwise retained, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain Cognitive Alpha Mining through code-based LLM evolution, a seven-level agent hierarchy and quality checking, with claims of predictive strength, stability and interpretability. The expanded dataset evidence supports these retained claims without introducing a different principal contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the Alpha360 stability explanation with an argument that more factors need not improve prediction, and explains Random Forest's RankICIR advantage through stability. New passages discuss market-dependent thresholds and hyperparameter diversity. The Limitations section adds specific qualifications concerning simulated trading, stochastic reproducibility and computational scaling.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: 20-factor combinations, rolling step 126, LightGBM/Ridge hyperparameters, runtime and single-H100 details, specific leakage checks, additional data sources, and MarketCycle plus crossover/mutation prompts. These mostly document previously described procedures. The abstract's promise to release all source code disappears, although the future prompt-repository statement remains; neither PDF provides a CogAlpha repository link.

R1.justification: v2 adds Verbalized Sampling (Zhang et al., 2025) to motivate generation diversity, together with Hong Kong index and yfinance references. The principal related-work coverage and positioning against formula-based alpha mining and evolutionary LLM research remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local rewrites clarify the meaning of cognitive reasoning, revise the baseline discussion and correct author/prompt terminology. Supporting material is reorganized into expanded appendices, and Limitations and Ethical Considerations sections are added.

P2.justification: The document switches from a single-column layout to two columns, extensively reflowing text, equations, code and prompt boxes. Table 1 gains dataset/horizon columns and comparator rows; Tables 4–5 and Listings 4–6 are added. The hierarchy diagram, ablation table, threshold plot and existing evolution listings move into appendices while retaining their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow CSI300 validation and lack of evaluated competing alpha-mining frameworks through Tables 1 and 5. The new sensitivity study and detailed implementation/prompt appendices strengthen empirical scrutiny and reproducibility, while the corrected Random Forest comparison improves accuracy. Uncertainty remains unquantified and the blanket code-release promise is removed, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial validation and documentation gains.
